channel.title: COSC — Foreigners' law updates (EN)
channel.description: Changes in Polish law on foreigners and official communiqués — from the Foreigners' Affairs Service Centre.

item.title: Ban on staying near the border with Belarus to apply for another 90 days from 30 November 2026 – Ministry of the Interior draft in consultation
item.description:
On 10 November 2026 the Ministry of the Interior and Administration (Ministerstwo Spraw Wewnętrznych i Administracji, MSWiA) sent for inter-ministerial agreement and public consultation a draft regulation extending the temporary ban on staying in a designated area of the border zone at the border with Belarus. The current regulation (Dz.U. 2026 poz. 1129) applies until 29 November 2026; the new one is to enter into force on 30 November 2026 and apply for 90 days. The area of the ban does not change: a 78.29 km section of the border in the Podlaskie voivodeship, within the range of the Border Guard (Straż Graniczna) posts in Michałów, Narewka, Białowieża, Dubicze Cerkiewne and Czeremcha – along 59.24 km a 200 m strip from the border line, along 15.26 km in the area of nature reserves and the Białowieża National Park approx. 2 km, and along approx. 3.79 km approx. 4 km inland. In the justification the ministry states that from the beginning of 2026 until 8 November, 482 attempts to cross the border in breach of the rules were recorded. The ban does not apply, among others, to persons permanently residing, performing paid work or running a business in that area (art. 12b ust. 1 of the act on the protection of the state border – ustawa o ochronie granicy państwowej). General rule: the ban applies to everyone, regardless of the residence title held, and only until the date indicated in the regulation – a further period requires a new act published in the Journal of Laws (Dziennik Ustaw).
Source: Ministerstwo Spraw Wewnętrznych i Administracji (legislacja.gov.pl) More & contact: https://cosc.org.pl/aktualnosci.html?lang=en&utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=aktualnosci-en • WhatsApp +48 539 999 549

item.title: Return proceedings against 25 foreigners and a fine for the employer after an inspection of a plant near Olsztyn
item.description:
The Border Guard (Straż Graniczna) initiated proceedings on obliging 25 foreigners to return after inspecting a production plant in Olsztyn county (9 November). Of more than 100 persons checked, 23 were working without the required permits (citizens of Nepal, Georgia, Colombia, Indonesia and Sri Lanka), and two were staying in Poland illegally. The inspection also covered 3 employment agencies that had sent the workers to the plant. According to the Border Guard, the employer faces a fine of up to PLN 50,000 – art. 84 ust. 1 of the act of 20 March 2025 on the conditions for entrusting work to foreigners (ustawa o warunkach dopuszczalności powierzania pracy cudzoziemcom, Dz.U. 2025 poz. 621) provides for a fine of PLN 3,000 to 50,000 for illegally entrusting work, and for a foreigner performing work illegally (art. 84 ust. 2) – a fine of not less than PLN 1,000. General rule: working without the required permit or declaration means a risk of a return decision for the worker and a penalty for the entity entrusting the work, also when the worker was sent by an agency.

item.title: Frontex return operations in Poland: the Sejm accepted all Senate amendments, the act has gone to the President
item.description:
On 6 November 2026 the Sejm considered 6 Senate amendments (print no. 3275) to the act amending the Border Guard Act (ustawa o Straży Granicznej) and certain other acts. Motions to reject them did not obtain the required absolute majority, so all amendments were adopted (print no. 3321). On 9 November the act was sent to the President for signature. It adds art. 329b to the Act on Foreigners (ustawa o cudzoziemcach), under which the Commander-in-Chief of the Border Guard will be able to ask Frontex to organise or coordinate return operations and interventions in Poland. One amendment provides that authorisation to use direct coercive measures, weapons and ammunition is granted by the Commander-in-Chief of the Border Guard with the consent of the minister for internal affairs. After signature, the act will enter into force 14 days after publication. General rule: enforced return decisions may also be carried out with the participation of European return teams.
Source: Sejm RP More & contact: https://cosc.org.pl/aktualnosci.html?lang=en&utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=aktualnosci-en • WhatsApp +48 539 999 549

item.title: The Sejm agreed to extend, from 17 November 2026, the restriction on applying for international protection at the border with Belarus
item.description:
On 6 November 2026 the Sejm approved the Council of Ministers' request (print no. 3276) to extend the temporary restriction on the right to apply for international protection at the state border with Belarus: 425 MPs voted in favour, 17 against, 1 abstained. The restriction is to be extended from 17 November 2026 for another 60 days, under art. 33a(3) of the Act of 13 June 2003 on granting protection to foreigners (Dz. U. z 2026 r. poz. 862). The previous extension resulted from the Council of Ministers' regulation of 15 September 2026 (Dz. U. poz. 1217). The next step is a new regulation of the Council of Ministers. According to the justification, between 27 March 2025 and 15 October 2026 applications from 496 foreigners were not accepted, while applications from 201 persons from so-called vulnerable groups were accepted. General rule: the restriction applies only to the border with Belarus and always for a fixed period; each extension, for at most 60 days, requires the Sejm's consent.
Source: Sejm RP More & contact: https://cosc.org.pl/aktualnosci.html?lang=en&utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=aktualnosci-en • WhatsApp +48 539 999 549

item.title: Requests to punish employers and return proceedings after checks on legal employment in Pomerania
item.description:
Court requests to punish employers, fines and return proceedings: these are the results of legal employment checks by the Maritime Branch of the Border Guard (Straż Graniczna), announced on 3 November 2026. At a construction site in Gdańsk five foreigners (from Azerbaijan, Georgia, Uzbekistan and South Africa) were found working without the required permits; return proceedings were opened against them and a request to punish the employer for illegal entrusting of work will be filed with the court. In Gdynia, 23 of 30 persons checked were working illegally; according to the Border Guard, the company's management board president, a Ukrainian citizen, did not have the required permit to hold that position and received two fines totalling PLN 2,000, and return proceedings were opened against him and five other foreigners. In a transport company from the Słupsk district the employer failed to report that a Moldovan citizen had started work (fine of up to PLN 1,000), and in another transport company 13 Belarusian citizens worked on terms different from those in their declarations; a request to punish the employer was filed. A request for punishment or opening of proceedings does not yet determine liability. General rule: the Border Guard pursues not only work without a permit, but also work on terms different from the declaration and failure to meet the reporting obligation; the employer is liable for an offence and the foreigner risks an obligation to return.
Source: Straż Graniczna More & contact: https://cosc.org.pl/aktualnosci.html?lang=en&utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=aktualnosci-en • WhatsApp +48 539 999 549

item.title: MOS outage on 27–28 October: applications filed by 2 November deemed filed on 27 October (art. 225c of the Act on Foreigners)
item.description:
On 3 November 2026 the Office for Foreigners (Urząd do Spraw Cudzoziemców) announced that on 27 October at 18:25 the MOS (Moduł Obsługi Spraw) portal stopped accepting applications and the fault was fixed on 28 October at 8:36. Under art. 225c(1) of the Act of 12 December 2013 on foreigners (Dz. U. z 2025 r. poz. 1079 z późn. zm.; provision added by the act of 21 November 2025, Dz. U. poz. 1794), applications filed via MOS from 28 October to 2 November by foreigners for whom 27 October was the last day of legal stay are deemed filed on 27 October. This concerns applications for temporary residence, permanent residence and EU long-term resident permits. The provision allows filing until the 3rd working day after the day the fault is fixed, and the Head of the Office for Foreigners announces the fix on the office's website. In a separate notice of 9 November the Office stated that possible short unavailability of the Trusted Profile (Profil Zaufany) on 12 November between 22:00 and 23:00 is not a system malfunction within the meaning of the act and does not shift deadlines for filing via MOS. General rule: an MOS outage on the last day of legal stay does not take away the right to file, but the application must be filed no later than the 3rd working day after the fault is fixed.
Source: Urząd do Spraw Cudzoziemców More & contact: https://cosc.org.pl/aktualnosci.html?lang=en&utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=aktualnosci-en • WhatsApp +48 539 999 549

item.title: Frontex return operations in Poland: the Senate has made 6 amendments to the adopted act, now it is the Sejm's turn
item.description:
On 22 October 2026 the Sejm adopted the act amending the Act on the Border Guard (ustawa o zmianie ustawy o Straży Granicznej oraz niektórych innych ustaw) (druk nr 3146; 251 MPs in favour, 144 against, 41 abstained). On 27 October the Senate made 6 amendments to it (druk nr 3275), which on 28 October were referred to the Sejm Committee on Administration and Internal Affairs. The act adds art. 329b to the Act on Foreigners (ustawa o cudzoziemcach): the Commander-in-Chief of the Border Guard (Komendant Główny Straży Granicznej) will be able to request the Frontex Agency to organise or coordinate return operations and return interventions on Polish territory, and tasks related to returns will also be carried out by officers of other EU states and Frontex standing corps staff. The Senate amendments add, among other things, ust. 5a: authorisation to use means of direct coercion, weapons and ammunition (art. 82 ust. 8 of Regulation (EU) 2019/1896) is granted by the Commander-in-Chief of the Border Guard after obtaining the consent of the minister responsible for internal affairs. After the Sejm considers the amendments and the President signs it, the act will enter into force 14 days after its publication. For a foreigner with a return decision (decyzja o zobowiązaniu do powrotu), this means that its forced enforcement may also be carried out with the participation of European return teams.
Source: Sejm RP More & contact: https://cosc.org.pl/aktualnosci.html?lang=en&utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=aktualnosci-en • WhatsApp +48 539 999 549

item.title: Week in review: draft new rules on recognition as a Polish citizen and a request to extend the asylum restriction on the border with Belarus (25–31 October)
item.description:
Law: on 27 October, draft UD491 amending the Polish Citizenship Act (ustawa o obywatelstwie polskim) was published in the list of legislative work of the Council of Ministers (Rada Ministrów). For recognition as a Polish citizen it provides, among other things, for a longer period of legal residence, a civic test and knowledge of Polish at B2 level instead of B1; the government plans to adopt the draft in Q4 2026, and until then the Act of 2 April 2009 applies (Dz. U. z 2025 r. poz. 1611). On 29 October the Council of Ministers asked the Sejm (druk nr 3276) to consent to extending, from 17 November 2026, for another 60 days, the restriction of the right to apply for international protection on the border with Belarus; the request awaits the Sejm's decision. No new acts on the stay and work of foreigners were published in the Journal of Laws (Dziennik Ustaw) this week. Life in Poland: at a processing plant in Łomża county the Border Guard (Straż Graniczna) checked the identity of 87 foreigners and detained 32, and 8 people received return decisions (zobowiązanie do powrotu). In the investigation by the Rzeszów-Jasionka Border Guard Post into false certificates of study submitted to voivodeship offices (urzędy wojewódzkie), a total of 23 people have been charged; a charge does not mean a conviction. In Małopolska, return decisions with a ban on entry to the Schengen area were issued to, among others, foreigners working without the required permit and a person whose temporary residence application was left without consideration. On the border with Lithuania, almost 900 foreigners have been refused entry since the beginning of the year; temporary border control applies there until 30 March 2027. In practice: submit a complete residence application while your stay is legal and only with genuine documents, because an application left without consideration does not protect you from a return decision.
Source: Kancelaria Prezesa Rady Ministrów, Sejm RP, Straż Graniczna More & contact: https://cosc.org.pl/aktualnosci.html?lang=en&utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=aktualnosci-en • WhatsApp +48 539 999 549

item.title: Draft UD491: longer residence, Polish at B2 level and a civic test for recognition as a Polish citizen
item.description:
On 27 October 2026 the draft act amending the Act on Polish citizenship and certain other acts (UD491), prepared by the Ministry of the Interior and Administration (MSWiA), was published in the Council of Ministers' list of legislative work; its adoption by the government is planned for Q4 2026. For recognition as a Polish citizen (uznanie za obywatela polskiego), the draft provides for a longer minimum period of legal residence in Poland (the list does not state the new length), a declaration of loyalty to the Republic of Poland, a civic test on knowledge of Poland, centre of vital interests and tax residence in Poland, a minimum income, a legal title to housing and a source of livelihood for all applicants, and raising the required level of Polish from B1 to B2. Mandatory grounds for refusal are planned, including a final conviction, fines or penalty tickets within a specified period before the application, false data and forged documents. For restoration of citizenship, the procedure under art. 38 of the Act is to be phased out – applications may be filed until 31 December 2030. The draft also allows a decision on recognition as a citizen or restoration of citizenship to be revoked at any time if it was obtained on the basis of forged documents or false statements, including those made in residence proceedings or proceedings for the Pole's Card (Karta Polaka). This is the stage of assumptions – the current rules are those of the Act of 2 April 2009 on Polish citizenship (Dz. U. z 2025 r. poz. 1611).
Source: Kancelaria Prezesa Rady Ministrów – wykaz prac legislacyjnych More & contact: https://cosc.org.pl/aktualnosci.html?lang=en&utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=aktualnosci-en • WhatsApp +48 539 999 549

item.title: Inspection of legal employment at a processing plant: 8 return decisions and proceedings against 24 more foreigners
item.description:
Eight return decisions (zobowiązanie do powrotu) and return proceedings against the remaining detainees – this is the result of an inspection by the Border Guard (Straż Graniczna) Post in Białystok (Podlasie Border Guard Division) at a processing plant in Łomża county, announced by the Border Guard on 30 October 2026. According to the statement, foreigners working at one site named eight different entities as their employers; the Border Guard opened an inspection of the legality of employment against each of them, while checking the legality of stay in nearby towns. 87 foreigners had their identity checked and 32 people from Colombia, Vietnam, Guatemala, Indonesia, Kenya, India, Zimbabwe, Peru and Nepal were detained. About 50 Border Guard officers and a Police patrol took part; the inspections are ongoing and, according to the Border Guard, the findings so far indicate a number of irregularities regarding the legality of foreigners' work. General rule: when work at one plant is performed for several entities, each of them is responsible for the legality of entrusting work, and a foreigner without a title to stay or work risks a return decision – regardless of who is formally their employer.
Source: Straż Graniczna More & contact: https://cosc.org.pl/aktualnosci.html?lang=en&utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=aktualnosci-en • WhatsApp +48 539 999 549

item.title: 800+ for a foreigner without a job: three statutory exceptions and the dispute with ZUS
item.description:
Since 1 February 2026 a foreigner must be professionally active to receive the child-raising benefit (świadczenie wychowawcze) (art. 1 ust. 2a ustawy z 11 lutego 2016 r., t.j. Dz.U. z 2026 r. poz. 508). The Act provides three exceptions, and the administrative courts read them more broadly than ZUS: in their view, a disability certificate for one child releases the parent from this condition also with regard to the other children. We explain the provision, the dispute and the deadlines for an appeal.

item.title: 300 zł for a child's school kit — who is entitled
item.description:
The „dobry start” benefit (300 zł) is also available to foreigners, but what decides is the basis of stay, not citizenship. For most non-EU workers the deciding document is a residence card (karta pobytu) endorsed “access to the labour market” — a work visa alone is not enough. Since 1 July 2026 (Dz.U. 2026 poz. 866) people under temporary protection must additionally meet an economic activity condition. Applications are filed online only and only until 30 November. Own material of COSC.
Source: Centrum Obsługi Spraw Cudzoziemców (materiał własny) More & contact: https://cosc.org.pl/artykul-300-plus-wyprawka-szkolna-cudzoziemcy.html?lang=en&utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=aktualnosci-en • WhatsApp +48 539 999 549

item.title: Who may represent you in a residence card and work permit case
item.description:
In residence card and work permit cases the representative (pełnomocnik) may be any natural person with full legal capacity — no professional title is required (art. 33 § 1 k.p.a.). A title becomes necessary only before the administrative court (art. 35 § 1 p.p.s.a.), and a cassation complaint to the NSA requires one (art. 175 § 1 p.p.s.a.). A separate part covers the risk when an agency or an employer files on the foreigner's behalf: letters from the office then go to the representative (art. 40 § 2 k.p.a.), and after a change of employer a request may go unanswered and the application may be left without examination (art. 64 § 2 k.p.a.). Own material of COSC.
Source: Centrum Obsługi Spraw Cudzoziemców (materiał własny) More & contact: https://cosc.org.pl/artykul-adwokat-czy-radca-prawny-sprawy-cudzoziemcow.html?lang=en&utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=aktualnosci-en • WhatsApp +48 539 999 549

item.title: The single permit directive — what Poland has yet to implement
item.description:
On 15 July 2026 the European Commission called on 17 member states, Poland among them, to implement Directive (EU) 2024/1233 on a single residence and work permit; the transposition deadline passed on 21 May 2026. Poland already has the single permit itself (art. 114 of the Act on foreigners), but differs in the detail: protection after losing a job lasts 30 days (art. 123(1)) against 3 months in the directive, and 6 months where the permit has been held for over 2 years. Own material of COSC with a comparison of the provisions.

item.title: Four times higher funds required to enter Poland — MSWiA draft
item.description:
A draft regulation of the MSWiA (no. 1351 in the list of legislative work, published 14.10.2026) raises the funds required on entry: from 75 to 300 zł per day, from 300 to 1000 zł for a stay of up to 4 days, and for study and research purposes from 1270 to 2020 zł. The requirement does not apply to people entering on a residence card or on a visa issued for the purpose of work (art. 25(3) of the Act on foreigners). This is a draft — the current amounts still apply. Own material of COSC.

item.title: How much a bailiff may take from your pay in 2027
item.description:
From 1 January 2027 the minimum wage will be 4950 zł gross (Dz.U. 2026 poz. 1213), and with it rises the amount free from deductions — about 3703,93 zł net on a full-time contract. The limits on seizure are 50% of pay for ordinary debts and 60% for maintenance, while on a bank account 75% of the minimum wage is free, that is 3712,50 zł. Citizenship does not change these rules. Own material of COSC with a step-by-step calculation.

item.title: Accident of a seasonal farm worker — KRUS, ZUS and the farmer's liability insurance
item.description:
After an accident on a farm three parallel routes are open: a one-off compensation from KRUS (1431 zł for each 1% of impairment), benefits from ZUS (1781 zł for each 1% from 1 April 2026) and civil claims against the farmer's liability insurance (OC rolnika). Citizenship does not decide the right to benefits, but in KRUS insurance the basis of stay and the title to work do matter. Legal status: October 2026.

item.title: MOS: an application for a residence permit for a child or ward requires creating a sub-account first
item.description:
The Office for Foreigners (Urząd do Spraw Cudzoziemców) reminds applicants (notice of 7 October 2026) that to submit in the Case Handling Module (MOS – Moduł Obsługi Spraw) an application for a residence permit for a child or ward, you must first create a sub-account for them. After logging in to MOS, go to “My account” – “Personal data” and, in the section for children/wards’ accounts, choose “Add account”. Only then can you submit the application on behalf of the child or ward. Practical rule: a parent or guardian should create the sub-accounts before preparing the applications, so as not to lose time when filing documents.

item.title: About 130 sham companies and nearly 11,500 declarations on entrusting work to foreigners: another charge in the Łódź investigation
item.description:
According to a Border Guard (Straż Graniczna) notice of 7 October 2026, in the investigation of the Regional Prosecutor’s Office in Łódź, conducted jointly with the Border Guard Unit in Łódź, another person (the fourth in the case), detained on 26 September, was charged with organising others’ illegal border crossing and obtaining a false certification by fraud; the court ordered three months’ pre-trial detention. The findings indicate that about 130 companies with no real business activity were set up in Poland, and through them nearly 11,500 declarations on entrusting work to foreigners were registered. Three people were detained in May 2026; the investigation is ongoing. Detention and charges do not mean a conviction. General rule: a declaration on entrusting work submitted by a company that does not actually operate does not create legal employment, and taking part in such a scheme entails criminal liability.
Source: Straż Graniczna More & contact: https://cosc.org.pl/aktualnosci.html?lang=en&utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=aktualnosci-en • WhatsApp +48 539 999 549

item.title: Obligation to submit the contract and penalties for illegally employing a foreigner in 2026
item.description:
New obligations: submitting the foreigner's contract to the office and notifying about the start of work. Fines of up to PLN 50,000, PIP (National Labour Inspectorate) penalty notices of up to PLN 10,000, joint inspections by the PIP and the Border Guard. Legal status as of 2026.

item.title: Legal stay does not give the right to work: return decisions and a one-year entry ban for three Colombian nationals
item.description:
The Border Guard (Straż Graniczna) post in Tarnów found three Colombian nationals in Bochnia County who were staying in Poland legally but working without the required work permits. Administrative proceedings were opened against them and ended with return decisions (zobowiązanie do powrotu) with a ban on re-entering Poland and the Schengen area for one year. According to the Border Guard's statement, the entity that entrusted the work without a permit faces a fine of PLN 3,000 to 50,000. General rule: a residence document does not replace a work permit or another legal basis for working — working without such a basis may lead to the loss of the right to stay and an entry ban.
